stories.detailText: Kristaps Porziņģis addresses ‘frustrating' health issue after Warriors meeting originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area Kristaps Porziņģis returned to the Warriors’ practice facility Tuesday, but his status remains the same. Porziņģis, who is dealing with an unspecified health issue and will miss all six of Golden State’s preseason games, met with general manager Mike Dunleavy and vice president of player health & performance, Dr. Rick Celebrini on Tuesday, the Warriors shared in a statement Wednesday. The details of that meeting will be kept private. Porziņģis hadn’t been around the team for weeks, and while he finally met with team staff Tuesday and intends to stay around the team, he will remain out indefinitely due to the same health-related matter. Warriors statement on Kristaps Porzingis: pic.twitter.com/Pdj4aM1Kes — Warriors PR (@WarriorsPR) October 14, 2026 Porziņģis wasted no time addressing the matter, sharing to X that he is working with doctors and experts to figure out how to get fully healthy and return to the court. “Honestly, I’m getting better and better,” he wrote, in part. “I just have to stay patient, and I believe I’ll be feeling great again soon.” He also took a subtle shot at the “internet doctors” who seemingly have diagnosed his health issue. I appreciate all the internet doctors trying to diagnose and help, but I'm in the best hands. So everyone can relax now 😄🙏🏼 and I don’t have hiv or aids. — Kristaps Porzingis (@kporzee) October 14, 2026 Porziņģis’ absence came as a surprise when Dunleavy announced it at media day, just before the team packed their bags for training camp in Hawaii. The 7-footer was seen working out at Chase Center before training camp, so Dunleavy’s announcement was a shock. The Warriors acquired Porziņģis from the Atlanta Hawks at last year’s trade deadline for Jonathan Kuminga and Buddy Hield. He averaged 16.1 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.1 blocks through 23.7 minutes in 15 games (11 starts) with Golden State, proving he can be an impact player for the Warriors when healthy. The Warriors already will be short-handed to start their upcoming campaign, with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody both recovering from long-term knee injuries. teamStories.summary: The Spurs enter the season with expectations to return to the Finals after their loss to the Knicks.
teamStories.detailText: IT'S A MUGGY Sunday in September at Frost Bank Center, and San Antonio Spurs media day is still a little more than two weeks away. As the sun peeks through the arena's east entrance, condensation trickles down the floor-to-ceiling windows, a testament to the 86% humidity outside and similar to the pressure cooker inside the building for fans vying for a spot on Victor Wembanyama 's official handpicked Spurs supporters group: the Jackals. "This is something that hasn't been done to this level," said Aidan Sterling, president of the Jackals. "All the people who weren't Jackals last year, all the new guys, I know there's nerves amongst them." Jitters would set in for some of the returning Jackals, too. Because unless they earned designation as "pack leader," membership isn't guaranteed this season, just like the Spurs aren't assured a spot in the 2026-27 NBA Finals after last season's shocking run that ended a six-year postseason drought and captivated fans. "There's a lot of competition," said one of the Jackals' pack leaders. "Being a part of it last season doesn't guarantee you a spot this year." It's a reality the Spurs understand all too well when measuring prospects for the upcoming season against the gauntlet that is the NBA's Western Conference, not to mention a vastly improved East or the fact that no team has advanced to the Finals in consecutive seasons since the 2018-19 Golden State Warriors . It's why Wembanyama and the rest of the squad tread carefully when discussing the sky-high expectations thrust upon the club in the wake of a 28-win improvement and Finals appearance. Wembanyama turned heads going into last season when revealing the team's goal of advancing to the postseason as a top-six seed. Then, at September's media day, Wembanyama mentioned, "I couldn't imagine better motivation" coming off a 4-1 series loss to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals. The 22-year-old was the only Spur that day to openly discuss specifics regarding expectations for the upcoming season. "We have some goals between us that we're going to keep between us as teammates," Wembanyama said. "We won the West last year. We don't want to do anything less this year. We want to be the first seed, and then we want to keep fighting for this top spot." To do that, San Antonio plans to lean on process to spin success the way it has done for decades. It's the approach the Spurs used last season, focusing on internal improvement and the day-to-day to help them manage an 82-game regular season and an extended postseason. In their minds, that's the only way to return to the game's grandest stage. It's a methodology dating to former coach Gregg Popovich's 29-season tenure in which San Antonio established a South Texas dynasty that churned out five titles and a record-tying run of 22 consecutive playoff appearances. At Pop's final media day as head coach during Wembanyama's second season, the Hall of Famer explained that, "even when we were a championship-caliber team, we never said we're going to win this many games. It was never a point of discussion." It still isn't, even with a new regime calling the shots. "Our expectation is to continue to try to improve and be the best version of this team we can be," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "The expectations are kind of like big games, right? There's added enthusiasm, excitement, criticism, opinion. I've been on both sides of it now in this league, and I'll take the expectations." AS PANDEMONIUM ERUPTED on the Frost Bank Center floor when the Knicks celebrated their first championship in 53 years, Wembanyama stoically scratched at the back of his head at a lectern just a few feet away, perplexed by how San Antonio fell short in a Finals series in which the Spurs held double-digit leads in every game. "[All] five games this series had the same scenario," Wembanyama said. "[It was surprising] how relentless we were in our mistakes, and [how] they were in punishing them." In the days that followed their loss, Wembanyama, his teammates and the coaching staff set upon the task of finding out why as they headed into the summer. Yet no one is willing to divulge exactly what they learned went awry in the Finals. "We have a lot of clarity on why we feel like we lost and what we can do to get better," said Spurs guard Stephon Castle , who is one-third of the Spurs' expected starting backcourt. Castle, De'Aaron Fox and rising second-year guard Dylan Harper , who shined against the Knicks in the Finals as a sixth man, played just 69 minutes together last season, including 25 in the Finals, and were outscored by 47 points in those minutes, according to ESPN Research. By comparison, the Spurs had a plus-9.4 net rating when Fox and Castle shared the floor in the regular season, plus-6.2 with Fox and Harper, and plus-11.0 with Harper and Castle. Internally, the Spurs have faith in the three-guard construction, believing Castle and Harper possess the size to consistently hold their own against wings. All three threaten opponents as penetrators able to drive into the paint at will. "We're very fortunate to have such a dynamic roster where you can really get creative in terms of puzzle pieces and how you want to build out the puzzle," Johnson said. "We saw it at times with the three guards in addition to what you can do around Victor. ... There's definite growth for those three guys just in terms of playing off each other and continuing to complement each other." New lead assistant Billy Donovan, who replaced Sean Sweeney when he took the head coaching job in Orlando, will be charged with fostering the on-court growth of the three guards when they're on the floor together. During the few brief portions of practice open to media, Donovan was working with Fox, Castle and Harper on the floor at the same time. "It's been great," Fox said. "One thing we've talked about is him being able to coach three guards at the same time. When he was [head coach] in OKC, he had Dennis [Schroder], Shai [Gilgeous-Alexander] and [Chris Paul]. So, he's been able to make it work. That team wasn't supposed to go to the playoffs at the time and then ended up playing well because they figured it out. That's one thing he's bringing to us." WEMBANYAMA WASTED NO time jumping back in the lab after San Antonio's Finals loss and looked to make the most of the shortest offseason of his young career. In addition to working with Hall of Famer Hakeem Olajuwon for the second consecutive summer, Wembanyama and several Spurs, including free agent addition Tobias Harris , visited Fox for workouts at his home gym outside Houston. "We had a long season, but you don't want to go the entire summer without being able to be around your teammates and getting in the gym together," Fox said. "Just being able to be around each other, I think, is big. We have a group of guys that like being around each other." Wembanyama tested that notion in August by inviting several teammates to Paris for more work on the court, in addition to sightseeing and fellowship. Wembanyama wanted his teammates to know where he came from to get to where he is now as a generational superstar. So, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and his teammates worked out at Palais des Sports Maurice Thorez, where Wembanyama's professional basketball career began as a gangly teenager with Nanterre 92. Wembanyama described the time with his teammates as touching, emotional even. "They were willing to make this trip, and they were also curious about what I wanted to show them," Wembanyama said. "So it matters because these people matter to me. This place matters to me. Having the two of them together is kind of the same as when family comes to visit here." Second-year forward Carter Bryant sat with Wembanyama on plane rides as a rookie last season, discussing "our personal goals, team goals, collective goals [and] off-the-court goals." He said he enjoyed the fellowship in France with his teammate, coming away impressed by how far Wembanyama has come, and how he has maintained humility, which has helped him to grow as a leader. "[It was big] for us to take the time out of our summers after we had been together longer than anybody, then come to his home and for him to educate us about where he's from, [to] just be around him in his element," Bryant said. "For him to get to that point and come back to where he started and then have the people around him that are like, 'Yo, next year we're going to take that next step.' Not too many people get that experience." In between the work on the court and deep conversations about what took place during the Finals, the Spurs in Paris broke bread together on multiple occasions, including one dinner on a riverboat on the Seine River with the Eiffel Tower as the backdrop. During the visit to Paris, Bryant and his girlfriend biked 32 miles one day. Veteran forward Harrison Barnes even set up a tour of the Louvre for the visiting Spurs. Wembanyama continued his summer work while his teammates visited Paris by taking Barnes with him to train with a French rugby club. There, the 7-foot-4 center said he worked to improve his balance. So, even after a season in which Wembanyama became the NBA's youngest and first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year, finished third in MVP voting and led San Antonio to the Finals for the first time in 12 seasons, Bryant couldn't help but marvel at Wembanyama's insistence on involving his teammates in his offseason work. "With a franchise like this, the biggest thing is family having each other's backs and understanding what we stand for as a unit," Bryant said. SAN ANTONIO UNDERSTANDS the challenge ahead of returning to the Finals. Even if the Spurs consistently play at their peak, forces beyond their control could derail everything. Injuries and the matchup against the upstart Spurs stopped the Oklahoma City Thunder last season from returning to the Finals. The Indiana Pacers ' bid for a return ended before the next season even began with Tyrese Haliburton tearing his right Achilles tendon in Game 7 of that series against OKC. Injuries also slammed the brakes on the 2024-25 Boston Celtics ' potential return to the Finals, while the 2024-25 Dallas Mavericks vanquished their prospects by trading away their best player, Luka Doncic . The last team to win the title after losing in the Finals the previous year was the Warriors, who used a once-in-a-generation cap spike to add Kevin Durant to a core that had already won a title in 2015. The Spurs' only notable free agent signing was Harris, a 15-year veteran who has never been beyond the second round of the playoffs. Still, the Spurs know they can't just jump straight back to the Finals to make up for the mistakes that cost them the series against the Knicks. Throughout the entire organization, everyone has bought in to the idea of taking everything one step at a time -- the same approach they used last season. "It's human nature, right," Spurs forward Devin Vassell said. "You want to be back in that situation, but you can't skip a day. You can't skip training camp. You can't skip the preseason. You can't skip opening night. You can't skip the lone back-to-backs. You can't sit here and snap your fingers [and] you're back in the Finals. It just doesn't work like that. Nothing is guaranteed. So, we've got to keep implementing what we were doing last year, stuff that carried over and just building good habits. We can't fast forward anything. So, just take it day by day." Veterans Barnes and Luke Kornet advanced to the NBA Finals at previous stops. Golden State captured a title in Barnes' first Finals appearance (2015) but fell the next season 4-3 to the Cleveland Cavaliers . Kornet, meanwhile, played for the Celtics in the 2022 Finals, which the Warriors won in six games, and returned in 2024, when the Celtics beat the Mavericks in five games to end a sixteen-year title drought, three years longer than San Antonio's current titleless run. "For us, it's a matter of focus that we have every single day in terms of what's our standard we're setting for ourselves and comparing it against that," Barnes explained. "I don't think it's one of those things where you simply carry momentum from one season to the next. You have to come back and start the journey from day one again. "I do think there's something that sharpens your focus, like shared heartbreak. And mind you, health is always a major factor. Those things are out of your control. But for the things that are in your control, having that experience helps you frame how you approach every single day." Several fans at the Jackals' tryouts could relate, showing their dedication in front of Sterling in a Chewbacca costume underneath a David Robinson jersey, and, of course, green alien garb. Meanwhile, San Antonio's alien, Wembanyama, and his teammates continue to temper expectations for the season. "This isn't pressure," Sterling said. "This is passion."

(Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The Buffalo Bills stole a soul-crushing win from the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5, reminding anyone still tuned in well past midnight on the East Coast that with quarterback Josh Allen, anything is possible. There were several heroes for Buffalo to embrace following the thrilling Monday Night Football win, from Allen, to outside linebacker Greg Rousseau, and a special teams unit highlighted by kicker Tyler Bass and his game-winning 48-yard field goal. Depending on your stance, you might even put running back James Cook III among the game’s heroes. Might… and why? It’s true that his fumbles have taken on a featured role in 2026, but it’s also worth wondering how many games they win this season with him on the sideline. That’s true of Week 4’s game. At 4-1, the Bills are in first place in the AFC East with a tenuous half-game lead over the 3-2 New England Patriots. Their only loss was to those Patriots, and it’s a situation where Buffalo must play their best football to maintain that lead throughout the season. Apart from Rousseau, the defense is a work in progress at best — while at times appearing to be a complete mess in trying to hold off opposing offenses. Buffalo currently ranks 30th in total defense, and 28th in points per game. The Bills also currently hold a turnover differential of -4, are they’re among the top-10 most penalized teams ( hat tip Trey Wingo ). There is a lot to work on, which you’ll hear ad nauseam from head coach Joe Brady and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. That, of course, must happen while managing injuries, which right now has Buffalo evaluating right tackle Spencer Brown, who couldn’t finish in LA thanks to a back injury. stories.title: Falcons QB Michael Penix on track to start vs. Bears if no setbacks, coach says
stories.summary: Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will start Sunday against the Bears despite a rib injury, as long as there are no setbacks during the week.
stories.detailText: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . will start Sunday against the visiting Chicago Bears despite a rib injury, as long as there are no setbacks during the week, coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday. Penix said he made every throw in practice Wednesday and took all the first-team reps. He was listed by the Falcons as a full participant in practice. In Sunday night's home loss to the Baltimore Ravens , Penix took a big hit late in the fourth quarter and came out of the game. He returned one play later, but when the tie game went into overtime, Tua Tagovailoa entered as the Falcons' quarterback. The Ravens scored a touchdown on their first drive in OT, and Tagovailoa threw a game-ending interception. Penix had imaging done earlier this week, but Stefanski said he didn't want to get into specifics about the extent of the rib injury. Stefanski said Penix is "feeling better." Penix also didn't want to get into the specifics of the imaging done, just that it was positive news. "They're good," he said of his ribs. "They get better every day. I felt good today at practice and I know I'm going to continue to feel good. I just got to stay on top of my rehab and just make sure I'm doing all the right things." Regarding snap share this week in practice, Stefanski said all of that will depend on Penix. "I want to see how he's feeling," Stefanski said. "With any injury like this, you want to make sure as they move around and how they're feeling -- it could be all, some, none. We shall see." Penix, 26, just returned to the Falcons' lineup in Week 3 after ACL surgery on his left knee last November. Without him and Tagovailoa (oblique) to start the season, the Atlanta offense, led by third-stringer Cooper Rush , scored a combined 16 points in two weeks. The following two weeks, with Penix back, the Falcons crushed the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints on the road, scoring a combined 80 points, a league high during that stretch.

stories.title: Patriots CB Gonzalez says he's 'ready to go'; WR Brown returns to practice
stories.summary: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez said Wednesday he's ready to return after missing the past two games with a shoulder injury.
stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez , who has missed the past two games due to a shoulder injury, said he will return for Sunday's home game against the New York Jets . "I'm good now, ready for Sunday," Gonzalez told reporters Wednesday. Gonzalez injured his shoulder in the team's Week 3 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and initially thought he was OK after the game. He explained Wednesday what unfolded in the days following the game. "At that point, you got a lot of adrenaline. Adrenaline covers a lot of things in this sport," he said. "At that time, I felt good. Things happen, so it is what it is and I'm ready for this week. "... I've been itching, kind of going a little crazy when I'm not getting to play. It's hard. You put in work with all these guys and then you don't get to be out there with them." Gonzalez watched the Patriots' 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders this past Sunday from the sideline, saying it was important to him to be there for his teammates. In addition to Gonzalez's return, receiver A.J. Brown is returning to practice for the first time since being placed on injured reserve Sept. 12, according to coach Mike Vrabel. This is the first day Brown is eligible to return and Vrabel said he would "see how that goes" before determining if Brown plays Sunday. Players were buoyed by news of Brown's return to practice. "Huge boost. He's a receiver one," veteran safety Kevin Byard said. "Obviously the past couple weeks our pass game has been playing really well so he adds another dynamic to that." In addition, second-year offensive lineman Marcus Bryant , who had been rolled up on in the preseason and was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return at the final roster cutdown, will also practice Wednesday. His return adds depth after starting left tackle Will Campbell was diagnosed with a sprained right MCL, a source told NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe. Campbell told reporters Wednesday that he was going to try to do some things at practice. Gonzalez, Brown and Campbell were all listed by the Patriots as limited participants in Wednesday's practice.

stories.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. ready for Texans debut alongside C.J. Stroud in a reunion with high stakes for both
stories.summary: For Stroud and Harrison, delivering on the hope of their reunion is integral to each of their NFL futures — not to mention the Texans' season.
stories.detailText: Marvin Harrison Jr. is ready to go. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters Wednesday that Harrison is in the game plan and will make his debut with Houston on Sunday, days after arriving via trade from the Arizona Cardinals . He's not expected to play a full allotment of snaps , but Harrison will be part of Houston's offense for Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. The game will mark the start of a reunion between Harrison and quarterback C.J. Stroud, who played with each to great success as college teammates at Ohio State. It's a reunion that comes with high stakes for both. Harrison and Stroud were elite together at Ohio State Stroud and Harrison were arguably college football's most dangerous pass-and-catch tandem during the 2022 season. Stroud was a Heisman Trophy finalist as he led the Big Ten in passing yards (3,688) and touchdowns (41). Harrison was an All-American as he tallied 1,263 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Ohio State advanced to the College Football Playoff semifinal, where it lost a 42-41 thriller to eventual champion Georgia. Stroud thew for 348 yards and four touchdowns. Harrison was on the receiving end of 106 of those yards and two touchdowns. Their success at Ohio State set them both up for great expectations in the NFL. The Texans made Stroud the No. 2 pick in the NFL Draft the following spring. The Cardinals selected Harrison at No. 4 in 2024 as a can't-miss NFL prototype at wide receiver. Since joining the NFL, neither player has met those expectations. Can C.J. Stroud and Marvin Harrison Jr. rekindle their success together that made them both elite NFL prospects? Tim Warner via Getty Images High stakes as Stroud hasn't secured contract extension Stroud got off to a strong start with one of the best rookie campaigns for a quarterback in NFL history that earned him Rookie of the Year honors after the 2023 season. But it's been a rocky road since. Stroud showed significant regression in his second NFL season as his touchdown-to-interception ratio plummeted from 23-to-5 to 20-12. He failed again in 2025 to match his rookie success, and his career reached a nadir in a 28-16 loss to the Patriots in the divisional round of the playoffs. Stroud threw four interceptions that day in a performance that would have gotten a lot of quarterbacks benched. But how do you bench a young quarterback in a playoff game if you're the Texans if you view Stroud as your future? Stroud finished the game. But he did not get an extension to his rookie contract in the offseason in his first season of eligibility to sign one. The message there is clear. The Texans have seen enough from Stroud to make them wary of investing in him in the long-term. They exercised his fifth-year option, and he's under team control through 2027. But the Texans need to see more from their fourth-year quarterback to sign him to a nine-figure deal. Harrison seeking to shed bust label As for Harrison, the prognosis is worse. Viewed as a lock for All-Pro success coming out of Ohio State, Harrison is instead flirting with a bust label. He was productive with 885 yards and 8 touchdowns as a rookie, but fell short of producing as an immediate difference maker in Arizona's offense. In his first season playing primarily with Jacoby Brisset at quarterback, Harrison regressed with 608 yards and 4 touchdowns in his second NFL season. Tight end Trey McBride, instead, developed into the go-to target in Arizona's offense while Michael Wilson leapt Harrison in the wide receiver pecking order. Through four games this season, Harrison virtually disappeared from the Arizona offense (5 catches, 85 yards, 1 TD) and the Cardinals gave up on him. It's rare for a team that invests in a high first-round pick to bail so quickly, but that's where the Cardinals landed, 33 games into Harrison's NFL career. With a second-round pick dangling in return, the Cardinals were happy to make him Houston's problem. And that's how Harrison ended up in Houston playing alongside Stroud for a 1-4 Texans team that's been one of the most disappointing in the NFL this season. But all hope isn't lost in Houston. Will reunion pay off for Stroud, Harrison, Texans? Stroud can't be blamed for Houston's early struggles. He's playing his best football since his Rookie of the Year campaign and will enter Sunday with a 64.3% completion rate and 280.4 yards per game on 7.6 yards per attempt. His next interception will be his first of the season. He's thrown for six touchdowns and run for another. His only turnovers through five games arrived on a pair of fumbles in Week 1 against the Bills. The plan with the Harrison trade is that his arrival will make him and Stroud better. With Nico Collins healthy and his favorite college target at his side, Stroud has every opportunity to continue his progression back to Pro Bowl form. With Stroud throwing the ball, Harrison can rekindle the form that made him a can't-miss prospect at Ohio State. And with a winnable slate of upcoming games against the Giants, Chargers, Browns and Colts, there's still time for Houston to turn its season around and contend for the playoffs. This is the hope, at least, in Houston. For Stroud and Harrison, delivering on that hope is integral to each of their NFL futures.

stories.title: Rico Dowdle injury updates: Latest status on Steelers RB foot injury
stories.summary: Jaylen Warren has carried a heavy workload in Dowdle's absence. He'll remain the lead back but could use some support from his teammate.
stories.detailText: Running back Jaylen Warren enters NFL Week 6 ranked third in the NFL in scrimmage yards with 640. The Pittsburgh Steelers would probably prefer for him not to be quite so prolific so early in the year. REQUIRED READING: Steelers PFF grades: Jaylen Warren's stats surging in Mike McCarthy offense The heavy workload that created that total has been a necessity because of the absence of Rico Dowdle, the veteran signed by GM Omar Khan this offseason to bolster the team’s depth at the position. Rico Dowdle injury update Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of a foot injury sustained against the New England Patriots, which included dislocating the same toe twice. “Rico is — he's been injured, but he looked good [Oct. 9 and 10],” McCarthy said in his weekly news conference Oct. 13. “He's definitely close to getting back there.” Dowdle was back on the practice field Wednesday in a limited capacity as the team geared up for the Week 6 matchup against the Tampa Bay Bucanneers. Pittsburgh Steelers running back depth chart Jaylen Warren Rico Dowdle Warren has handled the vast majority of carries in his place. Over the past three weeks, he’s taken 49 of the team’s 64 touches. To his credit, the production has been phenomenal. He had 194 yards from scrimmage in Week 3 against the Bengals; 126 in the Week 4 loss at Cleveland; and 188 in the Week 5 win against the Colts. The latter effort included an 80-yard touchdown catch and 50-yard touchdown run. It was the first such combo of explosive plays in the NFL since Herschel Walker completed it in 1986. Once Dowdle is back, McCarthy left little doubt about who will lead the backfield. “Jaylen is our featured player right now,” he said. “I mean, let's make sure we all recognize that. He's hot. He's playing great football for us. So, it's important for us, as an offense, coaches and players alike, to continue to put him in position to make plays. So that won't change.” Nevertheless, expect Dowdle to still have a significant role. The Steelers did not sign him to a two-year, $12.25 million contract to ride the bench. He’s been a 1,000-yard back each of the past two seasons. He was with McCarthy in Dallas in 2024 before having a nice year separately with Carolina in 2025. There’s also a need to be careful with Warren’s usage. At present, he’s on pace for a career high in carries, and that includes the first two weeks when he touched the ball less often. He’s simultaneously on pace for a career high in receptions as well. A 60-40 split in Warren’s favor seems like a fair expectation, with flexibility to lean harder on Warren as matchups and situations dictate built into McCarthy’s gameplan. stories.title: NFL survivor power rankings: Why you should use Rams, Patriots
stories.summary: ESPN NFL survivor pool strategy, predictions and picks for Week 6, including the Rams and Patriots.
stories.detailText: Welcome to ESPN NFL Survivor ! The rules are simple: Pick one NFL team each week to win its game. If that team wins (or ties), you advance to the next week. If that team loses, you are out. The catch is that each team can be chosen only once. ESPN's game requires just one team each week, so that will be the focus of this column, though I will touch on other major contests. For the third time in five weeks, the top-picked team in ESPN Survivor fell. This time, it was the Dallas Cowboys , who were picked by 35% of entries against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Since the loss came on Thursday, the concentrated selection on the Houston Texans and Cincinnati Bengals opened up other potential leverage opportunities. However, two of the top potential low-future value picks both tied or lost in the Washington Commanders and Atlanta Falcons . Luckily for those who play ESPN Survivor, Commanders backers advanced to Week 6, unlike in Circa Survivor or Splash Sports. Entering Week 6, only 9.7% of entries in ESPN Survivor remain. The biggest favorites in Week 6 are the Los Angeles Rams . While favorites of at least eight points are a paltry 5-5 outright, the four double-digit favorites this season are 4-0 outright. The Rams make a ton of sense as the biggest favorites of the week in their largest projected favorite role all season. However, Los Angeles is also projected to be favored in all but one or two of their remaining games, and as we get deeper into the season, having teams like the Rams available is valuable. That's especially true in Circa and Splash, which require multi-pick weeks, especially with the Rams projecting to be the biggest favorites on Circa's Thanksgiving slate. In contests that require one pick per week, the Rams are the optimal pick, especially in smaller groups that are unlikely to last all season. However, in large pools, and pools with multi-pick weeks, I prefer to save the Rams for later. The San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs are both laying over a touchdown, but they have the two lowest availabilities among all remaining teams (Chiefs 37%, 49ers 44%). Both are fine contrarian picks this week, though both have significant future value, especially the 49ers. The New England Patriots and Indianapolis Colts are the other strong choices this week. While they arguably have less win equity in Week 6, both have significantly less future value than the Rams, Chiefs and 49ers. However, both teams face the Dolphins in the next few weeks, so they will have other opportunities. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Future value based on Mike Clay's cheat sheet . 1. Los Angeles Rams (vs Cardinals) The Rams are the biggest favorites in the betting market by far in Week 6, and it's projected to be their largest favorite role all season. However, they are also projected to be one of the biggest favorites in each of the next three weeks (at Las Vegas Raiders , vs. Los Angeles Chargers , at Washington Commanders ), and they rank fifth in my future value model the rest of the season. Plus, on Circa, they play on both holiday slates, including a home game against the Green Bay Packers in the Thanksgiving slate. Ultimately, it comes down to what kind of Survivor player you are. Are you looking for the best pick in Week 6, or are you looking to map out your path for all 18 weeks? Chance to win: 88% (ESPN Analytics), 93% (Mike Clay) Spread: Rams -12.5 (-900 moneyline) Future value: Fifth Availability: 95% ESPN Selection: 33% 2. New England Patriots (vs. Jets) In larger groups, or contests with multi-pick weeks, the Patriots would be my top pick. While they have two games left against the Miami Dolphins , the home game doesn't come until Week 18, while the road game in Week 8 also includes the Cincinnati Bengals hosting the Tennessee Titans and the Dallas Cowboys hosting the Arizona Cardinals , two other very strong pivots. Outside of those two games -- and I don't worry about Week 18 this early in the season -- this is the best chance all season to use New England. The Patriots are 16-1 over their last 17 home meetings against the Jets, with the only loss coming in Bill Belichick's final NFL game. Just make sure to monitor the injury reports, especially on the Jets offense. Chance to win: 79% (ESPN Analytics), 75% (Mike Clay) Spread: Patriots -7.5 (-345 moneyline) Future value: 13th Availability: 96% ESPN Selection: 21% 3. Indianapolis Colts (vs. Titans) There are likely only two weeks all season where the Colts will be a strong favorite; this week, and Week 10 hosting the Dolphins. In a vacuum, the Dolphins matchup is better. However, with only 15% of ESPN entries on the Colts as of Tuesday evening, that Miami game looks like it will be the heavy chalk in Week 10. So if you are the kind of Survivor player who likes to fade the top pick each week, this is a great week to use the Colts in a great spot where they will be slightly lesser selected. Chance to win: 72% (ESPN Analytics), 77% (Mike Clay) Spread: Colts -7 (-340 moneyline) Future value: 17th Availability: 99% ESPN Selection: 15% 4. Kansas City Chiefs (vs. Chargers) Both the betting market and Mike Clay's model view the Chiefs as the second-biggest favorites this week. And since the Chiefs are available by only 37% of entries in ESPN Survivor, they are only projecting to be 5% picked. The Chiefs host the Jets and Cardinals in Weeks 9 and 11, but outside of that, they probably won't be usable again until the final couple weeks. However, in each of those weeks, there are several other strong picks, making this week stand out as a strong week to burn the Chiefs. Chance to win: 74% (ESPN Analytics), 93% (Mike Clay) Spread: Chiefs -8.5 (-500 moneyline) Future value: Fourth Availability: 37% ESPN Selection: 5% 5. San Francisco 49ers (vs. Commanders) The 49ers are now the Super Bowl favorites at DraftKings, and ESPN Analytics views them as the best team in the NFL. As a result, they rank highest in future value. Outside of Week 16 (at Chiefs), the 49ers will likely be favored in every game the rest of the season. Still, ESPN Analytics views this as the 49ers' easiest game the rest of the season, making this a fine week to burn them, especially since almost all the biggest favorites this week are some of the best teams in the NFL. Chance to win: 86% (ESPN Analytics), 86% (Mike Clay) Spread: 49ers -7.5 (-440 moneyline) Future value: First Availability: 44% ESPN Selection: 8% 6. Buffalo Bills (at Raiders) The Bills are only a consideration for me in Splash. While they are third in future value on ESPN, most of that value is in Week 11 hosting the Dolphins, where they will likely be one of the most popular selections all season. Their other easiest games are in Week 10 (at Jets), Week 17 (at Dolphins) and Week 18 (vs. Jets), none of which are double-pick weeks in the major Splash contests. Carter played 87 percent of the snaps in Week 5's tie with the Commanders, making five tackles (two solo) and picking up one sack. stories.title: Why Raheem Morris has quickly become a ‘great fit’ with 49ers as DC
stories.summary: The Niners DC has his unit playing like one of the best defenses in the NFL.
stories.detailText: The San Francisco 49ers have had a bevy of strong defensive coordinators in the Kyle Shanahan era. It all started with Robert Saleh, one of the best defensive minds in the NFL, who has since been hired as a head coach twice after stints in San Francisco. The 49ers then had DeMeco Ryans, who quickly established himself as a special defensive mind in his two-year stint as defensive coordinator. After two failed experiments with Steve Wilks and Nick Sorensen, and Saleh’s second stint last season, San Francisco had a vacancy at the coveted position again. A ton of names were floated around, but Kyle Shanahan and Co. focused on one: former Atlanta Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, who had been with Shanahan in Atlanta and Washington a decade ago. Morris had been an assistant in football since 1998 and a head coach twice, while having a ton of experience as a playcaller. Initially, despite all that, there were some who worried that the scheme difference could lead to some early growing pains. But through five games, Morris has been a fantastic addition, as several 49ers defenders are enjoying the best stints of their careers, while the unit as a whole has looked elite despite dealing with injuries. “It doesn’t surprise me with Raheem,” Kyle Shanahan said this week. “I’ve just been around him for too long. He’s one of the best people and best coaches I’ve ever been around. I tried to bring him here originally when I left Atlanta. They wouldn’t let him out. “So, it’s been a long time coming to get him here. He’s done an unbelievable job this year, especially with the injuries, but just overall everything he’s mixed up schematically. I love the confidence he’s given our DBs and the way they’ve been playing since training camp. He’s had a real huge effect on this team and we’re very lucky to have him.” The 49ers have been decimated on the defensive line. They ran it back with a secondary that was inconsistent last year. And they’re also relying on a good amount of young talent. Still, they rank third in EPA allowed per play, third in points allowed per game, and sixth in yards allowed per game. And that’s with the team facing the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Broncos, and Seattle Seahawks through the first five weeks. The 49ers’ defensive line personnel has been decimated. The team has been without Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Alfred Collins, Sam Okuayinonu, CJ West, and others for parts of the year. That’s prompted them to rely on a number of players who signed in training camp or later to play key snaps. And still, the group is producing. Osa Odighizuwa has been a very solid addition, leading the team with 15 pressures to go with a 12.8 pass-rush win rate on the interior so far. Keion White, a former New England Patriots second-round pick, has been a revelation. He’s second on the team in pressures (13) while recording eight defensive stops, good for fourth on the team. Gracen Halton has immediately stepped up as a rookie, and we’ve seen him get better each week. He had his best game yet against the Seahawks with three pressures and three defensive stops, along with a forced fumble. The same goes for both rookies Romello Height and Jaden Dugger, who had quality outings as well in Week 5. The veteran linebackers Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw have looked very good, with Warner seeming like a Defensive Player of the Year candidate once again, despite coming off a major injury. And the secondary has exceeded all expectations. Renardo Green and Malik Mustapha are having the best years of their careers. The group as a whole has looked very good in coverage, and they’re playing with a high level of confidence as Shanahan noted. Morris’s blitz packages have also given opposing quarterbacks trouble. But the key part is that he’s keeping things simple for his defense, which has allowed the group to pick things up faster and play freely with more confidence. The 49ers are averaging 17 pressures a game, despite their personnel, while also swarming to the ball and looking good in coverage. That’s got me thinking about how good Morris is relative to his predecessors, which is a very high bar to meet. So far though, he’s passed every test with flying colors.

stories.title: Week 5 3 up and 3 down: The Falcons lost as a team
stories.summary: Two defenders and the team’s top receiver turned in great weeks, while the coaching staff and a franchise legend deserve some criticism after Week 5.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons flips while hurdling Jaylinn Hawkins #21 of the Baltimore Ravens in the third quarter of a game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons blew it in primetime. It’s easy to handpick one or two plays, but this loss was a team effort. That said, there are still performances worth highlighting. Here’s the Week 5, 3 up and 3 down. 3 up Sydney Brown Brown has been one of Cunningham’s best additions . In Jeff Ulbrich’s scheme, the hybrid safety does it all, playing in the box like a LB and as third safety/big nickel in other packages. He has a nose for the football and has been one of the secondary’s more reliable tacklers. Brown has far exceeded expectations and is more than an upside special teams addition; he’s a critical piece of Ulbrich’s defense. The team should prioritize extending him if he keeps playing well. Sydney Brown is a spark plug pic.twitter.com/9jIfyPBwii — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 13, 2026 Jessie Bates III Bates delivered a vintage performance after a lackluster start to the season. He scored his first defensive touchdown of the season and had his best day in coverage. Bates kept the lid on the back end of the field, and while the Falcons couldn’t hold on to the lead, his play wasn’t the reason why. It’s good to see Bates hitting his stride because the secondary continues to take on injuries, and they have a Ben Johnson offense on deck. Drake London London is still Penix’s go-to target, and it’s easy to see why. When third down reared its ugly head, London routinely moved the chains. London was targeted six times on third down and hauled in five passes, moving the chains on each completion. We’d all like to see Penix spread the ball a bit more, but it’s nice to know he has a legitimate security blanket for the game’s toughest moments. Thanks to the Falcons play-action offense, London is finding himself in more space than ever , but he’s still getting the job done when he doesn’t have that space. Every Drake London 3rd down target from Week 5 pic.twitter.com/dgAC9LN37g — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 13, 2026 3 down Divine Deablo When asked about the Ravens putting up 208 yards on the ground, Deablo said, “Put it on me.” While no one player is entirely to blame, Deablo is right that he deserves a fair share of it. He turned in a rough performance. Deablo has been out of his gap too often and has struggled to diagnose plays at the speed we became accustomed to in 2025. The hamstring injury is definitely holding him back, but the linebacker often seems to be in his own head and tries to make a play instead of just doing his job. He has regressed this season, but he’s not far off from getting back on track if he can clean up these mental mistakes. Jake Matthews Father Time comes for us all. Yes, the dropped touchdown was bad, but bigger issues need addressing. Matthews looks like a sled on most of his reps, getting blown off the snap with ease in both the passing and running game. He was dealing with an injury all week, but this performance isn’t a one-off. It feels like he’s hanging on by a thread, and it’s always hard to watch a team legend not perform up to their standard, but most people can see now that upgrading the tackle position will need to be a priority this offseason. Rough outing for Matthews and the OL pic.twitter.com/jAAAOLMkVE — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 13, 2026 Coaching This was the staff’s first disappointing game of the season. Why call a passing play for Jake Matthews when he’s been dealing with a groin injury all week? How do you see Zachariah Branch turn a short pass into a big 1st down conversion and never go back to that well? On the other side of the ball, Jeff Ulbrich flip-flopped between soft zone and ineffective blitzes to protect the lead. We can give him grace, knowing he was dealing with an injury to CJ Henderson, but the calls still weren’t good enough. The Ravens made better adjustments at halftime, and the Falcons staff had little to no answers. A loss like this feels all too familiar for Falcons fans. Frustration is high, and the team is below .500, but they’re still 2-1 under Penix and should remain competitive game to game. Being competitive is only a moral victory, but the season is far from over.

stories.title: Will the Packers earn a playoff spot this year?
stories.summary: This week’s survey asks Packers fans just how much you believe in the team’s improved performance.
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, TX - JANUARY 14: Detailed view of the NFL Wild Card logo prior to an NFL wild-card playoff football between the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on January 14, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Packers fans and fans across the country. Playoffs? We’re talking about playoffs? Surely that will be the reactions of some readers who see the question in the headline of this article. But after five weeks have passed on the 2026 NFL season, the Green Bay Packers somehow sit in the #5 spot in the NFC. Their 3-2 record puts them in a tie with the Bears and Lions in the NFC North and the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC West, but Green Bay’s results to this point have them ahead of each of those teams on tiebreakers. What does that mean in week five? Realistically, it doesn’t mean much, aside from the fact that the Packers have managed to keep themselves afloat despite all of their issues over the first few games. During the current two-game winning streak, Green Bay’s offensive line has looked good enough to at least keep Jordan Love upright enough to lead a functional passing game. Now, with a pretty significant game looming against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, we want to know if Packers fans are feeling good enough about the team to project them to make the postseason when all is said and done. Surely the big win over the Bears last Sunday will boost fans’ overall confidence in the team, but is it enough to get you to believe that this is a playoff team? Let us know in the polls and comments below and we’ll be back to talk about the results later this week. Will the Packers make the playoffs? Are you confident in the Packers? stories.title: Michael Penix should be ‘good to play’ vs. Bears despite rib injury
stories.summary: Fingers crossed this holds through the week, but Falcons quarterback Michael Penix does expect to play on Sunday vs. the Bears.
stories.detailText: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If you’re like me, you watched the end of Ravens-Falcons on Sunday night with an overwhelming sense of dread. The moment Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. pulled that towel over his head on the sideline as the Ravens rolled in overtime, I knew the game was over. And I was very worried about Penix’s availability in the short term. Thankfully, Penix was able to practice fully on Wednesday. After practice, he noted that he made all of his throws on Wednesday. “They get better every day. I felt good today at practice,” Penix said. “… I just gotta stay on top of my rehab and just make sure I’m doing all the right things.” Penix would not elaborate on the nature of the injury (he was asked if it’s a bruised rib, and he said he didn’t want to get too specific). But he did tell us the MRI was positive. Thankfully, before I got a chance to, Marc Raimondi from ESPN clarified with Penix that the MRI was not positive for any type of injury, but the results of the MRI were positive for Penix’s chances to start agains the Bears on Sunday. “Positive means I’m good to play,” said Penix. Even though Penix felt good in practice, it wasn’t perfect. “It’s not always comfortable, but I made every throw today,” he said. During the limited portion of practice we are permitted to watch, Penix was definitely moving around well today. There wasn’t any noticeable hesitation or gingerness in his rib area as he worked through drills. One little bit of luck for Atlanta is the absence of Montez Sweat this week due to his suspension for violating the league’s PED policy . But Penix, while acknowledging the mark Sweat can leave on games, said that the rest of the defensive front in Chicago is also tough. “I feel like he is an impact player, so he makes impacts on games, but the next-man-up mentality in the league — I feel like the guys that’s right behind are almost as good. They’re very close. So it’s hard for us to try to say that that’s going to change much because of him being out.” We’ll see what the official injury report says about Penix when it’s released Wednesday, and we’ll continue to monitor his status through the week and heading into Sunday’s matchup against the Bears.

stories.title: Mike Tomlin's interpretation of players-only meetings: "I think you're dead"
stories.summary: "The fact that you hear about it is what makes it BS," Tomiin said on the New Heights podcast.
stories.detailText: The Cowboys' defense recently held a players-only meeting . It's a common technique for teams that are struggling. In the opinion of long-time Steelers coach Mike Tomlin, there's one clear conclusion to be drawn as to a team that feels compelled to have a players-only meeting. Asked for his thoughts on the topic during a visit to the New Heights podcast with Travis and Jason Kelce, Tomlin kept it short and not sweet. " I think you’re dead ," Tomlin said. Tomlin later offered a more specific assessment. "If it did occur, I'd like to not hear about it," Tomlin said. "The fact that you hear about it is what makes it BS." We can't recall ever hearing about a players-only meeting during Tomlin's 19 years with the Steelers. Which may be one of the reasons why the Steelers never had a losing season in nearly two decades with Tomlin at the helm. In any other context, the idea of those being led meeting in the absence of their designated leaders would be viewed as unusual. If the students meet without the teacher present or the workers meet without management around, it would be regarded as planning for a potential mutiny. Really, why would the players, students, workers feel compelled to come together in the absence of those who are supposed to be directing them? Especially when, as Simms said on PFT Live , there are plenty of meetings by the team, the offense/defense, and the various position groups. It's a manifestation of desperation. And it necessarily tells the world that the players believe the coaches aren't giving them the answers they need, so they're searching for answers of their own.

stories.title: Klint Kubiak: Ashton Jeanty will play Sunday
stories.summary: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty will play in Sunday's game against the Bills, coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday.
stories.detailText: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty will play in Sunday's game against the Bills, coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday. A report earlier in the day indicated the Raiders are considering sitting Jeanty to let his ankle and foot injuries fully heal. Kubiak disputed that. "He's playing," Kubiak said, via Sam Warren of TheAthletic.com. Jeanty injured his ankle in training camp, and he had the foot injury added to the Week 5 report. He was limited last Thursday and did not practice last Friday. A game-time decision, Jeanty played 32 of 60 snaps and had 10 carries for 27 yards and three catches for 50 yards. "He's starting to feel a lot better physically," Kubiak said. "I'm excited about giving him even more reps in practice and more full-speed reps." Jeanty has 88 carries for 291 yards and 22 catches for 215 yards and two touchdowns.

stories.detailText: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 11: Bhayshul Tuten of the Jacksonville Jaguars is tackled by Riq Woolen of the Philadelphia Eagles during the 2026 NFL London Games match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) | Getty Images This defense deserved a win. The Jaguars have a good offense, and they were always going to make some plays. But the Eagles repeatedly gave themselves a chance with outstanding individual performances, physical run defense, and some ridiculous goal-line stops. Once again, the other side of the ball let them down. Being at this game was awesome. The goal-line stand in the first half happened right in front of where I was sitting, and it was easily my favorite moment of the afternoon. You could feel the intensity. There has been criticism of this defense for being a little soft this season, and some of that criticism has been fair. There was nothing soft about those reps. This group came to fight. It was so cool to see. This was not a flawless performance. But when your offense produces 10 yards over 15 plays across four consecutive second-half punts, you are asking an awful lot of the defense. They kept coming up with stops anyway. Let’s get into it. Defense Jalyx Hunt was outstanding against the run in the first half. He was a big loss when he went down. The Jaguars use their tight ends heavily in the run game, which makes the edge defenders’ ability to handle those blocks particularly important. Hunt does not just hold his ground here. He knocks the tight end backward and disrupts the play before the runner has a chance to get going. This was not a one-off, either. Hunt did this multiple times before his injury, and the Jaguars struggled to establish their run game. The Jaguars finished with 36 yards on nine outside zone attempts, which is impressive considering this is a big part of the Jags’ offense, and the Eagles have struggled with outside zone runs at times this year. Hunt’s ability to defeat tight end blocks was a big part of that. Eagles' Defense All22 Thread vs. Jags. 1) I thought Jalyx Hunt was outstanding in the first half against the run. The Jags use their tight ends a lot in the run game, but Hunt blows up this play by knocking the tight end back. He did this multiple times in the first half, and… pic.twitter.com/oEgGZfBmTz — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Jalen Carter. My word. When he is healthy and moving like this, he is as good as nearly any defensive player in the league. The frustrating part is getting this version of him consistently, because health has been such an issue. Here, the quickness and violence were back, and the Jaguars had very few answers in the first half. His club move is such a weapon. He can knock a blocker off balance and get past him before the protection can recover. But what I particularly loved was the finish. Carter was not content to just sack Trevor Lawrence. He went after the football. Carter was wrecking the offense. 2) Jalen Carter, my word, was he good in the first half. When Carter is healthy, he is as good as nearly any defensive player in the league. His issue is just staying healthy. He wrecked the Jags' offense in the first half, with a number of quick pressures and 2 forced fumbles.… pic.twitter.com/PTY4N70Fo2 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Unfortunately, there were still some mistakes, and this was a really disappointing one. Both safeties came downhill, which left the Eagles without a deep defender to chase down Parker Washington. My assumption is that Michael Carter II should be playing as the single-high safety here, but I cannot be certain of the coverage. What we can say is that the defense ends up without the protection it needs behind the play. Andrew Mukuba’s aggression is also part of the issue. I have mentioned this repeatedly: he is very eager to come downhill, and play action is catching him out. Some of that comes from what the scheme asks him to do against the run. This scheme does ask safeties to fly downhill from depth vs. the run. But there has to be a balance, and I think Mukuba is too aggressive at times. 3) This play was really disappointing because it's not a play you associate with this defense. It's a weird coverage, because both safeties come downhill, so I'm assuming Michael Carter got it wrong and should be a single-high safety. Without him at deep safety, there's no deep… pic.twitter.com/0yGHHJ6GoZ — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Despite that rep, I thought the secondary’s communication was much better overall. The Jaguars used plenty of motion and switch releases to test how the Eagles pass routes off, and we didn’t see the same frequency of coverage busts that have hurt this defense in recent weeks. This third-down stop by Quinyon Mitchell is a fantastic example of playing the situation. One of the biggest changes was the use of dime personnel on third-and-long. That means six defensive backs, with Jihaad Campbell coming off, Kenny Moore II entering at safety, and Carter II moving to the slot. I liked it. I generally like getting more defensive backs on the field in obvious passing situations, provided they can communicate and play together. There is no point adding coverage players if everyone ends up confused about their assignments. Here, the group looked comfortable, and I thought the package worked well until Carter II got injured. 4) I thought the Eagles' communication in the secondary was so much better this week than in previous weeks. The Jags used a lot of motion and switch releases, but we didn't see as many coverage busts as in recent weeks. This is outstanding by Quinyon Mitchell on 3rd down, who… pic.twitter.com/gk6QvzdsbZ — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 How often do you see a defensive tackle loop all the way around the offensive tackle on a stunt and finish with a sack? Barely ever! The Jaguars actually pass this stunt off well. They do not leave Carter unblocked. He still gets around the corner because his athleticism and bend are ridiculous for an interior defensive lineman. That is what makes this rep so special. The protection can handle the exchange and still lose because Carter can turn the corner like an edge defender. Then he attacks the ball again and forces another fumble. This is an individual player producing something beyond what the design alone creates. Phew. 5) How many times do you see a T/E Stunt where the DT runs around the edge of the tackle and sacks the QB? Barely ever! The Jags actually pass off the stunt well, but Carter has the athleticism and bend to turn the corner like an edge defender and force another fumble. What a… pic.twitter.com/p28Ypuv1fI — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Cooper DeJean’s work against the run remains one of the biggest reasons I like him at nickel. DeJean’s ability to get involved physically gives the Eagles something valuable there. I thought he was excellent in that part of the game. But I cannot move past Carter’s club move on this rep. Look at how quickly he defeats the block and gets himself into the backfield. Defensive linemen that size are not supposed to move like that. When he is playing at this level, he changes what the entire front can accomplish. He was a joy to watch in the first half. 6) Cooper DeJean was excellent as a run defender in this game, and his play against the run has always been a reason why I am a fan of leaving him at the nickel position. However, this one is still about Jalen Carter's club move. Defensive linemen his size are not supposed to… pic.twitter.com/EU8dc3VADa — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Alright, one more Carter play. I have to. This goal-line stand was right in front of me, and the intensity of this rep was absurd. He attacks the double team and breaks through it with such aggression that the offense cannot establish the push it needs. This is a dominant defensive lineman at his very best. He took off his helmet after the play and smiled at the fans. He knew he was playing unbelievably well! I could see it in his demeanor. Hunt deserves a lot of credit, too. He crashes down and blows up the run, helping turn the backfield into a mess rather than allowing the Jaguars to build a clean path to the end zone. When the offense needs only a yard, that kind of immediate disruption is everything. This was an outstanding combination of interior penetration and edge play. This defense came to fight. Watching it happen live was so cool. 7) Alright, last time talking about Jalen Carter. This goal-line stand was right in front of where I was sitting, and it was easily the coolest moment of the game. Just look at how aggressive and physical Carter is at breaking through this double team. That's an absurd rep. Just… pic.twitter.com/WA8iCgss6Y — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 The coverage during these goal-line sequences was just as impressive as the work up front. The Eagles played some outstanding man coverage in the red zone, and the Jaguars repeatedly had nowhere to go with the football. Near the goal line, the offense has little space to work with, but the defense also has little room to recover from a mistake. These stats are a little skewed because the Eagles played man coverage heavily in the red zone, but against Cover 0 and Cover 1 combined, the Jaguars completed only one of 10 passes for 27 yards. That doesn’t mean the Eagles should only play man coverage, of course. But in these situations, the execution was excellent. You cannot ask for much better coverage than this. 8) The Eagles' man coverage in the red zone, on multiple goal-line reps in this game, was so good. The Jags just had nowhere to go with the football. You can't cover better than this. pic.twitter.com/6nDEBT1zt2 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 I had to include the fourth-down stop that finished this stand. Hunt again disrupts the run and forces the back outside, which gives Zack Baun the opportunity to make the play. Baun is ready for it. He breaks inside unblocked and gets into the backfield before the runner can escape. His quick reaction makes this look easy, but that is exactly what I like about it. He sees the play and goes. After the criticism this group has received for its physicality, this sequence was a pretty emphatic response. 9) Had to post this 4th down stop. Another fantastic job blowing up the run by Jalyx Hunt and forcing the back run outside, and then it's just all about Zack Baun. He's prepared for this, and he breaks inside unblocked and blows up the run in the backfield. This was so awesome to… pic.twitter.com/Yov5IcOgkI — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 The use of dime personnel became more difficult in the second half when Carter II went off injured. Vic Fangio wanted to keep using dime, so Jonathan Jones came in instead. I understand wanting to retain a package that had worked, but the replacement still has to execute the assignment. Here, Brenton Strange badly beats Jones on third down. This is a difficult route to cover because Jones has no help. The Jaguars create a demanding individual matchup, and they deserve credit for exploiting it. Even so, you want your veteran defensive back to make this more competitive. Injuries have repeatedly forced the Eagles to change their personnel this season, and this was another example of a good idea becoming harder to execute when a player went down. 10) The Eagles had an issue in the second half, as Michael Carter went off injured. Vic didn't want to stop using dime personnel, so he used Jonathan Jones instead. This route is very difficult to cover, as Jones has no help at all, but Brenton Strange badly beats him on 3rd… pic.twitter.com/3wtVC7SPKS — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 What a fantastic interception by Quinyon Mitchell. I have said that the thing holding him back from being recognized as a top-tier cornerback is his ball production, so it was awesome to see him finish this one. Lawrence underthrows it, and Mitchell takes advantage. You still have to locate the ball and catch it. He does both. He was outrageously good again. He was consistently doing his job at a very high level against a strong receiving corps, including Parker Washington, who is excellent. Arnold Ebiketie also deserves some credit here. He had to play more in the second half after Hunt’s injury, and I thought he showed up. Yes, he should beat a tight end as a pass rusher, but he did it here, and he had other impressive rushes later in the game. 11) What a fantastic pick by Quinyon! I have said that the only thing holding him back from being recognized as a tier 1 CB in this league is his ball skills, so this was awesome to see. He was so good all game, and he does a fantastic job picking off an underthrown Trevor… pic.twitter.com/Xkh6ULPWho — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Here is the coverage issue I still want to see fixed. Crossing routes against Cover 3 have been a problem for Fangio’s defense for a while, and the Jaguars had a lot of success attacking it in this game. They had a ton of success against the Eagles’ Cover 3 defense this week, and it was obvious on film. I am not blaming Campbell for this particular play. This one is not his fault. More generally, though, I don’t think he is especially effective as the middle hole defender because he doesn’t consistently anticipate what is developing behind him. I prefer this pass defense in split-safety coverages. I think the Eagles were too worried about the run and played too much single-high. The Jaguars found success there, and the Eagles need a better answer to those crossing routes. They happened on more than one occasion. 12) One thing that has been an issue with Vic's defense for a while now is crossing routes vs. Cover 3. It felt like the Jags had a lot of success against Cover 3 in this game. They are a much better pass defense when in split-safety coverages. I'm not blaming this on Jihaad… pic.twitter.com/N6M6dB5xNG — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Another outstanding goal-line coverage rep. This was such a big part of why the Eagles stayed in the game. The Jaguars could move the ball at times, but getting it into the end zone was a very different challenge. The coverage held up under pressure in the moments when there was no margin left. And look at Ebiketie’s rush. He fights through the chip and then works against the left tackle, rather than allowing that initial contact to take him out of the play. I thought this was one of his most impressive reps. The defense needed someone to contribute off the edge in the second half, and he gave them some good rushes. 13) Again, just an amazing coverage rep on the goal line, and check out the rush by Arnold Ebiketie! Fighting through the chip block and the left tackle very impressively. pic.twitter.com/23CE59CftC — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Unfortunately, we have to end here. Sometimes a good offensive player makes an exceptional play. Washington is a stud, and this one-handed catch downfield against Tariq Woolen is unbelievable. Woolen’s technique isn’t great, so I don’t want to pretend this is a perfect coverage rep. But he does recover into a decent position. Washington still makes the catch. This might be a touch harsh, but after the first 2 weeks of the season, when I was glowing with praise, I think Woolen has been a little underwhelming over the past 3 weeks. He has had mental and technical errors every week, which has resulted in good receivers beating him. That is part of playing a good offense. You can get close enough to contest the throw and still lose to an outstanding individual finish. The Eagles had things to clean up in this game, but I thought they played really well overall against a good offense. Washington makes a fantastic play in a huge moment. Sometimes you have to acknowledge that. 14) Well, we have to end here. Sometimes great players make great plays. Parker Washington is a stud, and he beats Tariq Woolen downfield with an unbelievable catch. Woolen's technique isn't great, but he ends up in a decent position. He can't stop Washington from making the… pic.twitter.com/YPu5pgevIE — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 13, 2026 Final Thoughts I came away from this game feeling much better about the defense. Both Jalen Carter and Quinyon Mitchell were dominant, and the goal-line stands were some of the most physical football this group has played all season. I liked the dime package, too, particularly the improved communication before the injuries forced more changes. There was plenty here to build on. It looked way more like a ‘Fangio defense’ than we have seen the past two weeks. This was a defense fighting hard against a good offense, losing players, and repeatedly being sent back onto the field because its own offense could not sustain anything. The Eagles cannot keep expecting this group to produce another goal-line stand or another turnover every time the game starts slipping away. They gave the offense enough chances to win. The offense wasted them. That is the theme of this one. Again. Thank you for reading! I’d love to hear your thoughts, so feel free to comment below and ask any questions. teamStories.detailText: The Raiders designated tight end Carter Runyon to return Wednesday, the team announced. It opens Runyon's 21-day practice window, and the team can activate him back to the active roster at any point in the next three weeks. Runyon went on injured reserve on Aug. 30 with an undisclosed injury after not playing in the preseason. He became eligible to return last week after missing four games. Runyon played 13 games last season, seeing action on 45 offensive snaps and 206 on special teams. He made two tackles and caught one pass for 3 yards.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are trying to be break a two-game losing streak against the Buffalo Bills at home Sunday. Here are three things to know about the 4-1 Bills: Josh Allen is a monster: The Bills’ quarterback could be on his way to another MVP season. He has thrown seven touchdown passes and has run for eight more this season. He leads all NFL players in rushing touchdowns. A week after getting shredded by Drake Maye in New England, the Raiders now have to deal with Allen. Not fun. James Cook is also dangerous: Cook has ran for, at least, 111 yards in three of the Bills’ five games. The Raiders have had issues stopping the run at times this season. While Allen is the centerpiece, the Raiders most focus on stopping Cook as well. Cook does have some ball-security issues as he fumbled twice in a Week 5 win over the Rams. The Raiders have had success forcing fumbles this season. They will go after Cook. Defense is struggling: Yes, the Bills can score in bunches, but they need it. The Buffalo defense has had big trouble under first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. Buffalo has allowed, at least, 29 points in four of their five games. Rams’ star receiver Puka Nacua had 17 catches for 138 yards in Week 5. Brock Bowers could go off.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier Wednesday, ESPN reported that the Las Vegas Raiders are considering giving starting running back Ashton Jeanty a week off to help him recover from ankle and foot injuries. Later Wednesday, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak swiftly shut down that notion. “He’s playing,” Kubiak said when asked about that idea. Kubiak also said Jeanty is “starting to feel a lot of better.” Kubiak suggested that Jeanty will practice fully this week as the Raiders prepare to host the 4-1 Buffalo Bills on Sunday as they try to snap a two-game losing streak. Jeanty was a game-day decision Sunday at New England after he missed practice time last week with a foot injury. He suffered an ankle injury in training camp. He has not missed any playing time this season. Meanwhile, as expected, starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway won’t practice Wednesday because he’s in the concussion protocol. His status for Sunday’s game is in question. Kubiak said the team hopes wide receiver Jalen Nailor returns to practice Thursday with hopes of playing Sunday. He missed the New England game due to a concussion. Also, the team opened the 21-day window to return from the injured reserve for deep backup tight end Carter Runyon. He has been out since early in training camp. Rookie offensive lineman Trey Zuhn returned to practice after missing Week 5 with a knee injury.
